title: What workplace violence prevention plan and training do Texas health facilities need?
description: Texas Health and Safety Code chapter 331 (SB 240, amended by SB 463): committees, written plans, annual training and 2026 coverage, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Texas Health and Safety Code chapter 331, added by Senate Bill 240 in 2023, requires hospitals, nursing facilities, home and community support services agencies, ambulatory surgical centers, freestanding emergency centers and mental hospitals to adopt a workplace violence prevention policy and plan. The plan must require at least annual violence prevention training or education for staff who provide direct patient care. Senate Bill 463 added more facility types, which had to comply by September 1, 2026.
keyTakeaways: SB 240 took effect September 1, 2023, and covered facilities had to adopt their policy and implement their plan by September 1, 2024.
Section 331.004(b)(3) requires training or education at least annually for health care providers and employees who provide direct patient care, and it may be folded into other required training.
Each facility needs a committee with at least one direct-care registered nurse, one direct-care physician (with an exception for some home health agencies) and, if practicable, one security employee.

SB 463 (2025) extended chapter 331 to intermediate care facilities for individuals with an intellectual disability and state supported living centers, and broadened the home and community support services agency category, with a compliance deadline of September 1, 2026.
Violations are enforced by the appropriate licensing agency as if the facility had violated its licensing law.
regulator: Appropriate state licensing agency under Health and Safety Code 331.006, principally the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
appliesTo: Hospitals licensed under Health and Safety Code chapter 241 and state-operated hospitals exempt from licensing; mental hospitals licensed under chapter 577
Nursing facilities and home and community support services agencies that employ at least two registered nurses; ambulatory surgical centers; freestanding emergency medical care facilities
From September 1, 2026: intermediate care facilities for individuals with an intellectual disability and state supported living centers

blocks.text: SB 240 created a statewide workplace violence prevention framework for health facilities. The bill added Subtitle H, Health Facility Employees, to Title 4 of the Health and Safety Code, with a new chapter 331, Workplace Violence Prevention. It was signed by the Governor on May 15, 2023, and took effect on September 1, 2023.

Section 2 of the bill gave facilities a year to comply: "Not later than September 1, 2024, a facility subject to Chapter 331 ... shall adopt a workplace violence prevention policy and adopt and implement a workplace violence prevention plan." Chapter 331 therefore has three building blocks: a committee (section 331.002), a written policy (section 331.003) and a written plan (section 331.004), with post-incident duties in section 331.005. This page states the position as at November 2026.

Texas does not set a fixed training length or curriculum. Compare the more prescriptive approaches in [New Jersey](/regulations/new-jersey-healthcare-workplace-violence-training) and [Washington](/regulations/washington-healthcare-workplace-violence-training).

blocks.title: Newly covered facilities: deadline has passed
blocks.text: Section 2 of SB 463 required a home and community support services agency, intermediate care facility or state supported living center that became subject to chapter 331 under the amendment to comply "Not later than September 1, 2026." As at November 2026 that deadline has passed, so those facilities should already have a committee, policy, plan and annual training in place.

The plan must "require the facility to provide at least annually workplace violence prevention training or education that may be included in other required training or education provided to the facility's health care providers and employees who provide direct patient care." That single clause, section 331.004(b)(3), is the whole statutory training requirement.

Three points follow from the wording. The audience is staff who provide direct patient care, so non-clinical staff are not covered by this clause, although a facility may choose to include them. The frequency is at least annual. And the content can be built into existing annual training rather than delivered as a separate course, which is useful for facilities that already run annual competency days. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

Because the statute does not list topics, the content should come from the plan itself. The other plan elements in section 331.004(b) give a sensible minimum: the facility's definition of workplace violence, the response and investigation system, physical security measures, how to report through the facility's occurrence reporting system, and the right to have patient assignments adjusted after abuse or threats.

blocks.text: Under section 331.002, the committee must include at least one registered nurse who provides direct care, one physician who provides direct care (not required for a home and community support services agency with no such physician on staff), and one security employee if any and if practicable. A health system may run one committee for several facilities if it develops a plan for each facility and keeps each facility's data distinct. At least annually, the committee must review and evaluate the plan and report the results to the facility's governing body.

sections.heading: What must facilities do after an incident?

blocks.text: At a minimum, the facility must offer immediate post-incident services, including any necessary acute medical treatment, to each provider or employee directly involved. Section 331.005 also bars a facility from discouraging staff from contacting or reporting to law enforcement, and prohibits discipline, discrimination or retaliation against anyone who reports an incident in good faith or advises a colleague of their right to report.

These rights belong in the annual training. Staff who do not know they may report to police, or who fear retaliation, are less likely to report, and under-reporting weakens the committee's annual review. Section 331.003 separately requires the policy to encourage confidential information to the committee and to protect those who provide it. See [how to convert policies into training](/guides/how-to-convert-policies-into-training).

Through facility licensing. Section 331.006 provides that "An appropriate licensing agency may take disciplinary action against a person who violates this chapter as if the person violated an applicable licensing law." The chapter defines "Commission" as the Health and Human Services Commission, and the workplace violence policy must "comply with commission rules relating to workplace violence."

Evidence of annual training for direct-care staff, the committee's annual evaluation report to the governing body, and incident response records are the core documents to have ready for a licensing survey. See [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Because chapter 331 lets violence training sit inside other annual training, Knowledge Foundry tags the plan's elements as discrete requirements, so a combined annual competency program can still show which direct-care roles covered each element and when. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does Texas require workplace violence training for all hospital staff?
faqs.a: Section 331.004(b)(3) requires at least annual training or education for health care providers and employees who provide direct patient care. Facilities may extend training to other staff, and many do, but the statutory requirement is aimed at direct-care staff.

faqs.q: Can Texas workplace violence training be part of annual competency training?
faqs.a: Yes. The statute says the training or education "may be included in other required training or education." The facility should still be able to show that the violence prevention content was covered for each direct-care employee each year.

faqs.q: Do Texas nursing homes have to comply with SB 240?
faqs.a: Nursing facilities licensed under Health and Safety Code chapter 242 that employ at least two registered nurses are covered. They had to adopt the policy and implement the plan by September 1, 2024.

faqs.q: Does chapter 331 set a minimum training length?
faqs.a: No. Unlike New Jersey's two-hour minimum, the Texas statute sets only frequency (at least annually) and audience (direct-care staff). Content and length are left to the facility's plan.
